eyebrow: Why one pattern doesn't cover the estate

steps.label: Dozens of interdependent services
steps.sub: not one app — the coordination problem multiplies with every service

steps.label: Mixed patterns by tier
steps.sub: core ledger active-active, batch systems cold, most things in between

steps.label: Failover domains
steps.sub: related services must fail over together, not independently

code:
Tier 0 — payments ledger:     active-active   (RTO: seconds,  RPO: ~0)
Tier 1 — checkout, pricing:   warm standby    (RTO: minutes,  RPO: <1 min)
Tier 2 — search, reco:        cold/backup     (RTO: hours,    RPO: 1 hr)
Tier 3 — internal reporting:  backup/restore  (RTO: days,     RPO: 24 hr)
caption: Each service gets the pattern its own RTO/RPO tier justifies — not the pattern that sounds most resilient.

eyebrow: When patterns collide at the boundary
code:
checkout (active-active, us-east + us-west)
   calls -> pricing-service (active-passive, us-east primary)

us-east fails:
  checkout already serving from us-west   -- fine
  pricing-service hasn't promoted yet     -- checkout calls into a dead region
caption: A service's effective RTO is bounded by its slowest dependency's RTO — not its own.
